title: Judge Decoding: Faster Speculative Sampling Requires Going Beyond Model Alignment

### Reasoning:

#### Purpose:
The contribution's purpose is to expose why speculative decoding achieves limited speedups, specifically due to its verification rejecting objectively correct but non-aligned draft tokens. None of the prior papers explicitly investigate or report this specific empirical relationship between speculative decoding's verification mechanism and its rejection of correct continuations. While many papers discuss speculative decoding's efficiency or acceptance rates (e.g., [5], [9], [15]), they focus on improving acceptance rates or efficiency rather than analyzing the rejection of correct tokens as a limiting factor. No prior paper establishes this relationship.

#### Mechanism:
The mechanism involves experiments probing the speculative decoding decision/verification mechanism, testing acceptance of high-quality drafts (GPT-4o outputs and human text) under standard verification. Papers such as [5], [9], and [15] perform detailed studies of speculative decoding mechanisms, including acceptance rates and draft verification processes. For example, [5] conducts over 350 experiments analyzing acceptance rates under different setups, and [9] explores factors limiting acceptance rates. These papers use similar experimental approaches to analyze speculative decoding mechanisms, making the mechanism covered.

#### Evaluation:
The evaluation design demonstrates that even powerful drafts (GPT-4o outputs and human text) cannot achieve high acceptance rates under standard verification, capping speedups. Papers like [5], [9], and [15] use similar evaluation designs, focusing on acceptance rates and efficiency under speculative decoding setups. For instance, [5] evaluates acceptance rates across different draft models and setups, and [9] analyzes acceptance rates under various conditions. The evaluation design (measuring acceptance rates and speedup limitations) is covered by these prior works.

#### Domain:
The domain is LLM inference acceleration via speculative decoding. All prior papers focus on speculative decoding as a technique for accelerating LLM inference, making the domain covered. For example, [1], [2], [3], [5], [9], and others explicitly address speculative decoding in the context of LLM inference acceleration.
